Below is a structured 12-week general fitness programme tailored for a 58-year-old male, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise with HR targets around 70% of age-predicted max (roughly 115 bpm), no Valsalva maneuvers, and no max lifts. It focuses on safe resistance training, aerobic conditioning, mobility, and recovery in a full gym. It’s designed to progress gradually in volume and intensity while staying within his cardiac clearance. Always have medical clearance on file and monitor symptom responses (fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain, dizziness). Stop and seek guidance if any red flags appear.

Important parameters
- Target intensity: moderate (RPE ≈ 12–14 on a 6–20 scale; talk test available; HR ~ 105–115 bpm during cardio, adjust to tolerance).
- HR: avoid reaching or exceeding 70% age-predicted max (~115 bpm). Use RPE and symptom monitoring to guide effort.
- Valsalva avoidance: exhale through exertion, breathe during lifts, use nasal or pursed-lip breathing if needed.
- No max lifts; avoid isometrics to failure; use controlled tempo.
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes; 5 minutes cardio at easy pace + dynamic mobility.
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes; gentle cardio and static stretches.
- Progression: increase sets/reps or weight gradually every 2–3 weeks, keeping RPE safe.

Program structure
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (split into two upper-lower sessions, alternating).
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and safety; Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload with moderate increases; Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and conditioning with slightly higher volume, still within safe ranges.
- Recovery: at least one full rest day between sessions; emphasis on sleep, nutrition, hydration, and gentle mobility on off days.

Phase 1: Foundation and safety (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish technique, build aerobic base, introduce resistance with light loads, ensure safe breathing and HR response.

Weekly layout
- Day 1: Upper body A + Core
- Day 2: Lower body A
- Day 3: Rest or light mobility
- Day 4: Upper body B + Core
- Day 5: lower body B
- Days 6–7: Rest

Sessions details
1) Upper Body A (Weeks 1–2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes easy cardio (bike or treadmill) + dynamic shoulder/arm mobility
- Push-pull circuit (2 sets, 10–12 reps, RPE 11–13)
  - Seated machine chest press
  - Seated row (machine or cable)
  - Dumbbell overhead press (light weight, seated)
  - Lat pulldown (assisted if needed)
- Isolation finishing moves: 1–2 sets of 12–15 reps
  - Cable triceps pushdown
  - Cable biceps curl
- Core: 2 sets
  - Plank: 20–30 seconds (progress 30–45 seconds as tolerated)
  - Bird-dog: 8–10 reps per side
- Tempo: controlled 2–0–2 (2 seconds eccentric, 0 pause, 2 seconds concentric)
- Notes: feet flat, neutral spine, exhale on exertion

2) Lower Body A (Weeks 1–2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes cardio + hip/knee mobility
- Exercises: 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps
  - Leg press (moderate load)
  - Seated leg extension (drop set not advised; keep moderate)
  - Seated or lying leg curl
  - Glute bridge (bodyweight or light weight)
- Optional balance/activation: calf raises 2 sets of 12–15
- Core: dead bug or side plank 2x20–30 seconds
- Tempo: 2–0–2
- Important: avoid heavy loads; no max effort

3) Upper Body B (Weeks 3–4)
- Push-pull circuit (2–3 sets, 10–12 reps)
  - Chest fly on machine or cable
  - Seated cable row
  - Dumbbell lateral raise (light)

- Finisher: light banded pulling/pushing for 1–2 sets of 12–15

- Goblet squat or supported squat (light)
- Leg extension/curl alternation: 2 sets of 12
- Hip hinge pattern:*

Include supervised cardio sessions

- Day 4: Upper B

- Increase sets from 2 to 3 on main lifts gradually

- Retain no max lifting; maintain controlled tempo

- Day 3: Rest or mobility
- Day 4: Upper B

Program specifics

  - Leg extension or squats variation

Cardio progression

- One session includes light intervals (e.g., 1–2 minutes at moderate pace, 1–2 minutes easy) within safe HR range
- One longer day (40 minutes at a comfortable pace) if tolerated

Recovery and nutrition
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night; emphasize consistency
- Nutrition: 
  - Emphasize fiber, lean protein, healthy fats
  - Maintain modest caloric intake appropriate for body weight goals and cardiac health
  - Hydration: 2–3 liters/day depending on activity

- Recovery modalities: light stretching, mobility work after workouts; optional light walking on rest days

Safety notes and considerations
- HR targets: use HR as a guide but not the sole measure of intensity; RPE and symptoms are primary during this phase.

- Reassess every 3–4 weeks: note RPE, HR response, ability to complete prescribed reps with proper form

Understood. Below is a single, cohesive 12-week program integrating all adjustments discussed: strength emphasis (including compound lifts with safe progressions), increased cardio for weight loss with HIIT thoughtful integration, end-of-program 5K testing plan, and a cardiac-health–focused nutrition framework. It’s written as a week-by-week, day-by-day schedule with exact exercises, sets, reps, tempo, and progression notes. All work stays within the client’s clearance: moderate-intensity, HR capped around 115 bpm, no max lifts, no Valsalva, and emphasis on RPE and symptom monitoring.

Client profile (recap)
- 58-year-old male, six months post-MI
- Cleared for moderate-intensity exercise
- HR target during cardio generally ≤ ~115 bpm (use RPE/talk test primary)
- No max lifting; avoid isometrics to failure; controlled tempo 2-0-2
- Full gym access (machines, free weights safe, with technique emphasis)
- Goals: rebuild strength (including squats/hip hinges where safe), improve functional capacity, support weight loss, end with a 5K time trial in Week 12

Program structure overview
- Frequency: 4 resistance days per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) with integrated cardio and optional HIIT in later phases
- Phases:
  - Phase 1: Foundation and safety with increased resistance volume and base cardio (Weeks 1–4)
  - Phase 2: Progressive overload with stronger emphasis on strength + higher cardio volume + light HIIT (Weeks 5–8)
  - Phase 3: Strength consolidation, conditioning, HIIT optional 1–2 days, 5K build and test (Weeks 9–12)
- Weekly layout (typical template)
  - Day 1: Upper A (strength emphasis) + cardio
  - Day 2: Lower A (strength emphasis, includes compound patterns as tolerated) + cardio
  - Day 3: Rest or mobility
  - Day 4: Upper B (strength emphasis) + cardio
  - Day 5: Lower B (strength emphasis) + cardio
  - Day 6: Optional cardio or HIIT (depending on fatigue and capacity)
  - Day 7: Rest

Important warm-up and safety norms (applied every day)
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes total
  - 5 minutes light cardio (bike, treadmill, or elliptical)
  - 3–5 minutes dynamic mobility for hips, shoulders, ankles
- Core activation: 5–10 minutes of light core and balance work before main lifts
- Breath control: exhale on exertion; avoid Valsalva; maintain steady breathing
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes light cardio + static stretches focusing on worked muscles
- Symptom checks: chest pain, dizziness, excessive breathlessness, or fatigue beyond expected—pause and seek guidance

Phase 1: Foundation and safety (Weeks 1–4)
Rationale: establish technique, build base endurance, safer progression to heavier compound movements later.

Weekly layout
- Day 1: Upper A Strength + Core
- Day 2: Lower A Strength
- Day 3: Rest or Mobility
- Day 4: Upper B Strength + Core
- Day 5: Lower B Strength
- Day 6: Rest or Mobility or Optional Cardio
- Day 7: Rest

Phase 1 details (Weeks 1–4)
Upper A Strength (Weeks 1–2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min cardio + dynamic upper body
- Main lifts (3–4 sets x 8–12 reps; RPE 12–14; tempo 2–0–2)
  - Seated chest press (machine)
  - Seated row (machine or cable)
  - Dumbbell overhead press (seated)
  - Lat pulldown (assisted if needed)
- Accessories/Core (2–3 sets x 10–15)
  - Cable triceps pushdown
  - Dumbbell hammer curl
- Core/balance: Pallof press or anti-rotation band holds (8–12 per side); Bird-dog 8–12 per side
- Cardio: optional 15–20 min after weights or on a separate day

Lower A Strength (Weeks 1–2)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min cardio + hip/knee activation
- Main lifts (3–4 sets x 10–12)
  - Leg press (moderate)
  - Lying leg curl
  - Hip hinge pattern: Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells or hip hinge
  - Glute bridge (bodyweight/light)
- Accessories: Calf raises 2–3 sets x 12–15
- Core: Dead bug or side plank 2×20–30s
- Balance: single-leg stance 2×20–30s per leg
- Cardio: 15–25 min, under HR ~115 or RPE 12–13

Upper B Strength (Weeks 3–4)
- Main lifts (3–4 sets x 8–12)
  - Chest fly (machine or cable)
  - Seated row
  - Dumbbell lateral raise (light)
  - Face pull
- Push-up variation (incline or wall): 2×8–12
- Core: Pallof press 8–12 per side; Side planks 20–30s
- Accessories: 2–3 sets x 10–12
  - Cable pull-aparts
  - Triceps pushdown
- Cardio: 20–25 min gentle intervals optional (1–2 min at RPE 14–15)

Lower B Strength (Weeks 3–4)
- Main lifts (3–4 sets x 8–12)
  - Split squat or step-up (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
  - Leg extension or lying leg curl
  - Glute bridge with tempo 2–0–2 or hip thrust light
  - Romanian deadlift with light weight
- Calf raises: 2–3 sets x 12–15
- Core/Balance: Side planks 20–30s; Pallof/anti-rotation 8–12
- Mobility: post-workout hip flexor/hamstring stretches

Cardio in Phase 1
- Sessions: 2–3 per week
- Duration: 15–25 minutes total; progress to 20–30 by Week 4
- Modes: cycle, bike, elliptical, treadmill walking
- Intervals: optional light intervals in Weeks 3–4 (1–2 min at RPE 14–15, 1–2 min easy)

Phase 2: Progressive overload with increased strength emphasis + cardio/HIIT (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: stronger resistance stimulus; more cardio to support weight loss; begin HIIT sparingly.

Weekly layout
- Day 1: Upper A Strength + Cardio
- Day 2: Lower A Strength + Cardio
- Day 3: Rest or Mobility
- Day 4: Upper B Strength + Cardio
- Day 5: Lower B Strength + Cardio
- Day 6: HIIT session option or Cardio Focus Day
- Day 7: Rest

Phase 2 details (Weeks 5–8)
Upper A Strength (Weeks 5–6)
- Main lifts (4 sets x 8–10)
  - Seated chest press
  - Seated row
  - Dumbbell overhead press
  - Lat pulldown
- Accessories (2–3 sets x 10–12)
  - Cable triceps pushdown
  - Cable biceps curl
- Core: Pallof press 8–12 per side; Dead bug 8–12
- Cardio finisher: 5–7 min light interval on bike

Lower A Strength (Weeks 5–6)
- Main lifts (4 sets x 8–10)
  - Leg press
  - Lying leg curl
  - Goblet squat or safety-bar squat (control depth)
  - Hip bridge or hip thrust
- Calf raises 3 sets x 12–15
- Core: Side planks 20–30s; single-leg deadlift pattern with light weight
- Post-workout mobility

Upper B Strength (Weeks 7–8)
- Main lifts (4 sets x 8–10)
  - Chest fly
  - Seated row
  - Dumbbell lateral raise
  - Face pull
- Push-up progression: incline to floor as tolerated; 2–3 sets x 6–12
- Core: Anti-rotation banded press 8–12 per side
- Cardio: 20–30 min; interval work optional (1–2 min at RPE 14–15 with 2–3 min easy)

Lower B Strength (Weeks 7–8)
- Main lifts (4 sets x 8–10)
  - Leg extension or squat variation (goblet to light bar)
  - Lying leg curl
  - Split squat or walking lunge (short step, light)
  - Glute bridge with tempo 3–0–2
- Calf raises 3 sets x 12–15
- Core/Bal: 2–3 sets; balance work
- Mobility work post

Cardio/HIIT integration Phase 2
- HIIT: 1 day per week maximum during Phase 2
  - Bike or elliptical: 6–8 cycles of 30s hard (RPE 14–15) + 90s easy; total 12–16 minutes
  - Alternatively: 8 × 20s hard, 60s easy
- Scheduling: place HIIT after an easier resistance day or after cardio? Prefer after lighter resistance days or on separate days to protect lift quality.
- Ensure total weekly cardio 20–30 min on resistance days plus 1–2 dedicated cardio days of 25–40 minutes (steady or intervals)

Phase 3: Strength consolidation, conditioning, and 5K prep (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: maintain strength while increasing conditioning; reach the 5K test readiness; optimize pacing strategies.

Weekly layout
- Day 1: Upper A Strength + Core + Cardio
- Day 2: Lower A Strength + Cardio
- Day 3: Rest or Mobility
- Day 4: Upper B Strength + Core + Cardio
- Day 5: Lower B Strength + Cardio
- Day 6: Optional longer cardio or HIIT as tolerated
- Day 7: Rest

Phase 3 details (Weeks 9–12)
Upper A Strength (Weeks 9–10)
- Main lifts: 4 sets x 6–10
  - Seated chest press
  - Seated row
  - Dumbbell overhead press
  - Lat pulldown
- Accessory: 2–3 sets x 8–12
  - Cable pull-downs
  - Triceps pushdown
- Core: Pallof press 8–12; Anti-rotation 8–12
- Mobility: 5 minutes post

Lower A Strength (Weeks 9–10)
- Main lifts: 4 sets x 6–10
  - Leg press or goblet squat
  - Lying leg curl
  - Split squat or lunge (short step)
  - Hip thrust
- Calf raises: 3 sets x 12–15
- Core/Balance: 2–3 sets 20–30s holds
- Mobility

Upper B Strength (Weeks 11–12)
- Main lifts: 4 sets x 6–10
  - Chest fly
  - Seated row
  - Dumbbell lateral raise
  - Face pull
- Push-up progression: incline to floor as tolerated; 2–3 sets x 6–12
- Core: 2–3 sets 8–12
  - Cable anti-rotation or Pallof press
- Conditioning: short cardio finish

Lower B Strength (Weeks 11–12)
- Main lifts: 4 sets x 6–10
  - Leg extension or squat variation
  - Lying leg curl
  - Step-ups or lunges (low step)
  - Hip thrust or glute bridge
- Mobility: hip and hamstring
- Balance: 2×30s per leg

Cardio progression and HIIT in Phase 3
- Cardio: Total weekly cardio 25–40 minutes on most days; include at least one longer day (40–60 minutes) if energy allows
- HIIT: Optional 1–2 days per week, with 1–3 intervals depending on tolerance; keep intervals short (30–90s) and easy recoveries
- Run-walk for 5K prep remains integrated as a gradual progression, with week-by-week build to continuous running if tolerated

5K time trial test day (End of Week 12)
- Prep: clinician check prior to test; ensure a thorough warm-up
- Test-day plan:
  - Location: safe flat course; consider a measured route (3.1 miles)
  - Equipment: proper shoes, water, a pacing plan
  - Warm-up: 5–10 min easy cardio; dynamic drills; progressive jog inside test window
  - Test: run-walk approach as needed; aim for consistent effort around RPE 14 (somewhere “somewhat hard but sustainable”)
  - Monitoring: watch for chest discomfort, dizziness, or undue fatigue; stop if any red flags
  - Cooldown: 5–10 minutes easy walking, light mobility
  - Post-test: record time, RPE, and any symptoms; reflect on pacing and tolerance

Nutrition framework integrated across 12 weeks
- Goals: support training demands, promote weight loss if desired, maintain cardiovascular health
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day; up to 1.4 g/kg/day on heavier training weeks if tolerated
- Carbs: emphasize complex carbohydrates around workouts; distribute evenly across meals
- Fats: 25–35% of calories; emphasize unsaturated fats; omega-3 sources 2–3x/week
- Sodium: 1500–2300 mg/day, adjust per clinician guidance
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day; adjust for climate and exercise volume
- Meal timing: pre-workout snack (carbs + protein) if needed; post-workout protein within 1–2 hours
- Food quality: emphasize whole foods; limit ultra-processed items, prioritize vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grains, lean proteins
- 5K prep nutrition: ensure adequate energy around long cardio days and tests; avoid large meals immediately before intense runs

Tracking and safety
- Weekly check-ins: RPE tracking, symptom review, resting HR if available
- Progression: increase loads by small increments (2.5–5%) when technique remains solid and RPE stays within target
- If fatigue or symptoms worsen: add an extra rest day, reduce volume for a cycle, and consult the clinician
- Documentation: keep a simple log of workouts, loads, reps, cardio minutes, RPE, and symptoms

Grocery and equipment notes
- Equipment: prioritize machines or guided free-weight movements for safety; use dumbbells, machines, and a safety rack when introducing any balance-dependent squats or deadlifts
- Grocery focus: emphasize protein sources (fish, poultry, legumes, low-fat dairy), high-fiber carbs (vegetables, fruit, whole grains), healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, seeds), and low-sodium options

If you’d like, I can produce:
- A precise week-by-week day-by-day calendar with exact reps/sets per exercise, cardio minutes, and HIIT slots tailored to your client’s equipment and preferences
- A complete 2-week rotating grocery list and a 7-day sample menu aligned to his energy and macro targets
- A test-day protocol and a post-test recovery plan with pacing cues and a reconditioning plan after the 5K trial

Would you like me to generate the finished, fully detailed calendar now? If you share his exact height/weight, any dietary restrictions, equipment availability, and preferred exercise selections (or any injuries), I’ll tailor the numbers precisely and deliver a ready-to-use plan.
